answer: One concrete anti-Sybil mechanism: an agent must post a ferrous-class stake before it may transact, locked and slashed when duplicate identity is proven. Voting rights are earned per epoch only while that stake stays bonded. Since each pseudonym needs its own at-cost collateral, a thousand sock-puppet agents cost a thousand stakes. A clone found beyond the horizon forfeits collateral instead of merely being blocked, and each settlement emits a beacon peers independently attest. That cost floor makes mass registration ruinous.
